📋 Executive Summary

This report presents a complete static security analysis of the PragatiX / SPDMS MySQL database SQL dump exported on August 6, 2026. The scan covered 180 SQL files across schemas, data, and tables folders, covering 60 database tables.


The overall Security Score is 87/100 — indicating several high-priority findings around data integrity, schema design, and dump security settings that should be addressed before the next production release.


Key Findings:
  • Schema denormalisation — The students table stores 7 columns as both a raw value and a FK reference (year, semester, section, gender, academic_year, phone, DOB — all duplicated). This is the highest-volume schema issue.
  • Test data in production dump — Users with phone numbers 123, 1234567890, and fictional accounts (luffy, Elon Musk, Steve Jobs) exist alongside real student records.
  • FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 — FK checks are globally disabled during the entire dump import, which is a medium-to-high integrity risk.
  • DROP TABLE in dump — All schema files begin with DROP TABLE IF EXISTS, creating risk if the dump is accidentally replayed on a live database.
  • BCrypt passwords confirmed — All passwords are properly BCrypt-hashed ($2a$10$…). ✅ POSITIVE FINDING.
  • NULL-capable username/email on users table — MySQL's UNIQUE KEY allows multiple NULL rows, which can be exploited for authentication bypass.
Positive Findings ✅
  • ✅ BCrypt hashing ($2a$10$) used consistently
  • ✅ InnoDB engine with FK constraints
  • ✅ utf8mb4 charset throughout
  • ✅ Proper AUTO_INCREMENT PKs on all tables
  • ✅ UNIQUE constraints on email & reg_no
  • ✅ created_at / updated_at audit timestamps
  • ✅ Proper CASCADE / RESTRICT FK rules
  • ✅ No EXEC/sp_executesql (no dynamic SQL)
  • ✅ No plaintext secrets in schema DDL

High unknown Foreign Key Checks Disabled 00_ALL_TABLE_DATA.sql 16 
/*!40014 SET @OLD_FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=@@FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS, FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 */;

💡 Recommendations (Priority Order)

  1. P1 — Critical Fix NULL-capable username/email on users table. Add NOT NULL constraints; audit for existing NULL rows and backfill or delete them.
  2. P2 — High Remove test/fictional data from production dump. Delete rows with phone=123, phone=1234567890, fictional usernames before any production promotion.
  3. P3 — High Resolve denormalised columns in students table. Remove duplicate VARCHAR shadow-columns (DOB/date_of_birth, phone/phone_no, year/year_id, etc.) and derive values via FK joins.
  4. P4 — High Guard DROP TABLE statements. Wrap all DROP TABLE statements with an environment check variable or move to a separate DDL migration file distinct from the data dump.
  5. P5 — Medium Re-enable FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS during import. Run a post-import FK integrity check: SELECT * FROM information_schema.INNODB_SYS_FOREIGN_COLS.
  6. P6 — Medium Replace ENUM columns with lookup tables. Convert academic_year ENUM to a reference table to avoid DDL migrations for every new year.
  7. P7 — Medium Consolidate INSERT statements with explicit column lists. Update all dump INSERT statements to include column names for forward compatibility.
  8. P8 — Low Enforce phone number format CHECK constraint. Add CHECK (LENGTH(phone) >= 10 AND phone REGEXP '^[0-9]+$') to both students and users tables.
  9. P9 — Low Standardise column naming to snake_case. Column DOB should be renamed dob or removed in favour of date_of_birth.
  10. P10 — Info Strip sensitive metadata from exported dumps. Remove GTID_PURGED, AUTO_INCREMENT values, and SQL_LOG_BIN settings from dumps shared outside the ops team.

High users `username` Allows NULL users.sql 1 
[Schema analysis of `users`]
Description`username` is UNIQUE but DEFAULT NULL — NULL is not unique in MySQL; multiple rows can have NULL username.
ImpactAuthentication bypass: a user with NULL username may match multiple accounts.
RecommendationSet username NOT NULL; enforce non-empty value at application layer.
High users `email` Allows NULL users.sql 1 
[Schema analysis of `users`]
Description`email` is UNIQUE but DEFAULT NULL — same NULL uniqueness loophole as username.
ImpactMultiple users can have NULL email; password reset flows break.
RecommendationSet email NOT NULL.
Medium users `password` VARCHAR(150) users.sql 1 
[Schema analysis of `users`]
DescriptionBCrypt hashes are 60 chars (cost-10) but Argon2 / bcrypt-higher-cost hashes can reach 95+ chars. VARCHAR(150) is borderline.
ImpactFuture algorithm upgrades may exceed column length causing silent truncation.
RecommendationExpand to VARCHAR(255) to future-proof.

DescriptionBoth `assigned_academic_year` and `academic_year` ENUM columns are present on the users table.

High users `username` Allows NULL users.sql 1 
[Schema analysis of `users`]
Description`username` is UNIQUE but DEFAULT NULL — NULL is not unique in MySQL; multiple rows can have NULL username.
ImpactAuthentication bypass: a user with NULL username may match multiple accounts.
RecommendationSet username NOT NULL; enforce non-empty value at application layer.

Medium users `password` VARCHAR(150) users.sql 1 
[Schema analysis of `users`]
DescriptionBCrypt hashes are 60 chars (cost-10) but Argon2 / bcrypt-higher-cost hashes can reach 95+ chars. VARCHAR(150) is borderline.
ImpactFuture algorithm upgrades may exceed column length causing silent truncation.
RecommendationExpand to VARCHAR(255) to future-proof.
